title: Atomicity, visibility and the right counter

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, many threads run `counter++` on a shared `volatile int counter`. What does `volatile` give that counter?

options.text: Atomic updates, but no promise that other threads see them
options.says: The page says volatile provides visibility only, and counter++ on it is still not atomic.

options.text: Visible writes, but no promise that updates are atomic
options.says: The page says synchronized gives atomicity and visibility while volatile only provides visibility.

options.text: Private copies, merged into one total when threads end
options.says: The page describes per-thread copies for ThreadLocal on 5.3.1, not for volatile; volatile makes each write visible to others.

questions.stem: Per this page, when is a `LongAdder` the better choice for a shared total than an `AtomicLong`?

options.text: When threads need compareAndSet on the running total
options.says: The page says to use AtomicLong when you need compareAndSet or get-and-set.

options.text: When threads need the exact total after every update
options.says: The page says to use AtomicLong when you need the current value right after an operation.

options.text: When threads update the total often and all at once
options.says: The page says to prefer LongAdder over AtomicLong under high contention, because it stripes updates over cells.

concepts: LongAdder beats AtomicLong under heavy write contention, while AtomicLong is for compareAndSet and exact current values.
Atomicity and visibility are separate: synchronized gives both, volatile gives only visibility.
